angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 775,596 km at 102.72 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.7353 +/- 0.0109 mas (same row, RUWE 0.89): 102.72 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.115 (1.092 to 1.137) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 775,596 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.058 (1.017 to 1.098) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5960 +/- 15.7 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 1999550886837136640: teff_gspphot 5959.609 K (16th-84th percentiles 5942.1216-5973.5527), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 1999550886837136640: teff_gspphot 5959.609 K (16th-84th percentiles 5942.1216-5973.5527), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kronos.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.368, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
